title: PATE: Proximity-Aware Time Series Anomaly Evaluation

problem.claim: Time series anomaly detection algorithms require evaluation that reflects temporal dynamics and anomaly characteristics.

gap.claim: Traditional performance metrics assume iid data and do not adequately capture early or delayed detections and other temporal characteristics of anomalies.

contributions.claim: Introduces PATE, an anomaly evaluation metric that incorporates the temporal relationship between prediction and anomaly intervals.
Uses proximity-based weighting around anomaly intervals and computes a weighted area under the Precision and Recall curve.
Applies PATE to evaluate state-of-the-art anomaly detectors across benchmark datasets.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe PATE as a novel evaluation metric.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets reportedly show that PATE provides more sensible and accurate evaluations than other metrics.
The authors report that Point-Adjusted F1 Score fails to characterize detection performance well.
The authors report that PATE enables a fairer model comparison.

narrative_sequence.summary: Reliable evaluation of time series anomaly detection is important for decision-making in real-time and data-driven domains.
Existing metrics assume iid data and miss temporal effects such as early and delayed detections.
PATE evaluates the temporal proximity between predictions and anomaly intervals using buffer-zone weighting and a weighted precision-recall area.
The method is tested with synthetic and real-world datasets and with state-of-the-art anomaly detectors on benchmark datasets.
The authors report that Point-Adjusted F1 is inadequate for characterizing performance and that PATE supports fairer model comparison.

source_observation.claim: Evaluation metrics for temporal anomaly detection should account for the proximity between predictions and anomaly intervals.

interpretation.claim: Metrics that encode temporal relationships may distinguish detection quality more meaningfully than metrics based on iid assumptions.

application.claim: When comparing time series anomaly detectors, consider proximity-aware metrics alongside conventional metrics.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how PATE behaves across anomaly types, domains, or evaluation settings beyond the reported datasets.

unknowns: No formal definition of the proximity weights or buffer zones is provided.
No dataset names, quantitative results, baselines, or statistical analyses are provided.
No details are given about the anomaly detectors, experimental protocol, or limitations.
